subject: H() causes system hang for some short wav files, why?

messages.author: d5a56bc471a8bbda
messages.subject: H() causes system hang for some short wav files, why?
parts:
Hi all,

First off, thanks for providing such a fantastic piece of software and user community.  I'm a PhD student at University of California - Santa Cruz working on the interface of soundscape ecology and conservation.  Most of my background is the acoustic monitoring of elusive and rare birds.  On to my issue; I am trying to calculate entropy on a number of recordings and am getting a hangup on the one I've attached, I think the process in which I generated the files led to some other ones (simulated bird choruses in the style of Suer at al 2008) causing the same problem.  I'm pulling my hair out trying to figure out why I can't calculate entropy of this .wav.  By contrast I can draw up meanspec() and spectro() no problemo.  I've tried searching the group but can't seem to find a similiar issue.

The wave object is described as:
Wave Object
        Number of Samples:      2656154
        Duration (seconds):     60.23
        Samplingrate (Hertz):   44100
        Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
        Bit (8/16/24/32):       16 

Any ideas here?  I'm at a bit of a loss on how the sound synthesis would lead to this issue on some files but not others...

Thanks,
Abe Borker
NSF Graduate Research Fellow
UCSC Long Marine Lab
100 Shaffer Rd.
Santa Cruz, CA 95060

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] H() causes system hang for some short wav files, why?
parts:
Hi Abe,

I really couldn't tell you why there's a problem, but when I tested it, I also found that it hangs, even if I cut the file down.  However, simply passing it through a tiny trim in sox spit out a file that had no problems.  As a work around, I would suggest doing the sox trim on one of your files that works in seewave to begin with, then compare the outputs before and after the mini trim.  If they're the same or comparable, then you can simply mini trim your problem files in order to get them to work. Not terribly elegant, but might save you some hair :)

Steffi

Code:

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)

w <- readWave("~/Desktop/iter.1.alphdiversity.15.3.wav")
H(w)  #hangs
w1 <- cutw(w,from=0,to=1,output="Wave")
H(w)  #hangs

system("sox ~/Desktop/iter.1.alphdiversity.15.3.wav ~/Desktop/out.wav trim 0 60")
w1 <- readWave("~/Desktop/out.wav")
H(w1)  #[1] 0.808014

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] H() causes system hang for some short wav files, why?
parts:
Hi,

I am afraid this is an issue due to the way R uses memory.

R Wave objects might be very heavy as the original binary format is
converted into a hevary decimal format. The Wave object might then
take a great part of the RAM and do not let enough space for
computation.

If you have to do some stuff on .wav file as using the function H()
that requires to compute the STFT and the Hibert transform you might
exceed you RAM allocation and this leads to an R crash.

As suggested by Stefanie, a solution is indeed to split your files
and/or to compute the spectral (function sh()) and the temporal
entopries (function(th()) independtly and to manage properly your
different objects with the function rm().

For instance this might help:

rm(w)
H(w)

Jerome

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] H() causes system hang for some short wav files, why?
parts:
Well, I actually only split off about 0.23s of the file with sox to get
H() to run properly. On the other hand, when I split the file using cutw
all the way down to 1s, it still wouldn't finish the computation. So
while it might be a memory issue, I don't think it's not strictly
related to the file size.

I've had a similar problem in the past: I cut files using cutw() and
system("sox ...") down to the same size. However, files that I cut
using cutw took longer to analyze than files that had been cut with sox,
which was odd. I assumed it had something to do with the internal
arguments assigned to the files, but didn't really look into it any further.

Steffi
